linkedin.title: AI search is changing how we read the news, but not for the reasons you might think.
linkedin.body:
For years, we have trained ourselves to search for news like we search for products. We type a few keywords into a box, scan a list of blue links, and hope the right answer is somewhere in the first three results. It is a slow, manual process that treats news like static data rather than a flowing conversation.

AI changes that dynamic. Instead of hunting for the right article, you can now ask for the right context. You aren't just looking for a headline anymore. You are looking for the story behind the data, the perspective that matters to you, and the synthesis of multiple viewpoints.

The real shift here is moving from search to discovery. When we stop asking 'what happened' and start asking 'what does this mean for me,' the quality of our information improves. We stop chasing the same viral links as everyone else and start building a news diet that actually informs our decisions.

Of course, the technology is only as good as the sources it reads. The goal shouldn't just be speed. It should be clarity.

reels.title: A strange circle on satellite maps turned out to be a 390-million-year-old impact crater
reels.hook: A strange circle on satellite maps turned out to be a 390-million-year-old impact crater

beats.caption: A strange circle on satellite maps turned out to be a 390-million-year-old impact crater
That circle is the size of a large city.
beats.narration: That circle on the map is not a small town. It is the size of a large city.

beats.caption: An amateur astronomer found it by accident.
beats.narration: An amateur astronomer was searching satellite maps for a camping spot when they stumbled upon it.

beats.caption: It is a massive impact crater from space.
beats.narration: It turns out to be a massive impact crater, blasted into the Earth's crust ages ago.

beats.caption: This event happened 390 million years ago.
beats.narration: Scientists confirmed this impact occurred roughly 390 million years ago.

beats.caption: They found shatter cones in the rock.
beats.narration: They found shatter cones, which are rock formations created by extreme pressure, confirming the site's origin.

beats.caption: The crater is hidden in Quebec.
beats.narration: The crater is located in Quebec, sitting quietly on satellite maps until now.
